 Advertisement Some showers possible Thursday in Baltimore area, particularly south
 Advertisement Updated: 1:29 PM EST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ava Marie Meteorologist Some showers possible Thursday in Baltimore area, particularly south
 Updated: 1:29 PM EST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ava Marie Meteorologist BALTIMORE — Much-needed rainfall is forecast to develop for the Thursday morning commute with more to come, particularly to the south.
 || Closings/Delays | Weather Advisories | Radar | Forecast | Email Alerts | Send us your pics ||
Thursday will be cloudy, but still mild, with highs in the 70s. Rain showers are possible at times through Thursday night, possibly with isolated thunder, which could have an impact on the Ravens-Jaguars game in Baltimore.
 It will be cloudy around lunchtime across Maryland before showers pop up by evening, particularly in Southern Maryland and the Eastern Shore.
 The rain may not add up to much, a half-inch or less is expected for most of the Baltimore area, but it will break the streak of dry weather. The last time Baltimore got some rain was on Oct. 17.

 Alert Days vs. Impact Days 
 You may see the WBAL-TV 11 Weather Team highlight Alert Days or Impact Days in the forecasts. Here's what that means:
 An Impact Day is when weather will likely disrupt your normal daily schedule or routine.
 An Alert Day is when there's a threat of extreme, severe and possibly life-threatening weather.

 Advertisement Watch vs. Warning: Stay informed, understand the terminology
 Tropical storms and hurricanes each have two descriptors, a watch and a warning . Watches and warnings are issued in advance of the onset of tropical storm force winds (39-73 mph).
 WATCH : This means tropical storm or hurricane conditions are possible in the "watch area." A watch is issued up to 48 hours in advance of the onset of tropical storm-force winds.
 WARNING : This means tropical storm or hurricane conditions are expected in the "warning area." A warning is issued up to 36 hours in advance of the onset of tropical storm-force winds.
 What to do during tornado alerts
 WBAL-TV 11 Weather Meteorologist Tony Pann explains the difference between a Tornado Watch and Tornado Warning, and what you should do if one is issued.
 Get inside a sturdy home or building.
 Go to the lowest level, a basement, if available.
 No basement? Go to an interior room without windows or a hallway.
 Stay away from windows.
 WBAL Potential power outages
 Storm conditions could cause outages by knocking down tree limbs onto power lines and other electric delivery equipment. Baltimore Gas and Electric asks all customers to report their outage in any of the following ways: 
 Online, at BGE.com 
 BGE's free mobile app, available at the Apple Store or Google Play  
 Text message to 69243 
 Phone, by calling 877-778-2222 
 The latest outage information, including total number and general locations, is available on the BGE.com outage map .
 Fallen overhead power lines should never be approached or touched even if the lines do not appear to be live or sparking. Call BGE at 877-778-2222 to report fallen electrical lines, power outages and gas odors.
